newsitem.title: UK: Britain would be ready to send troops to Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Britain would be ready to send troops to Kuwait.

text.p: Britain told Kuwait on Tuesday it would be willing to despatch troops once more to the Gulf Arab state if necessary to deter Iraq.

Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said the recent thrust of President Saddam Hussein's forces in northern Iraq showed the international community needed to be on alert to respond to any Iraqi aggression or repression.
"The United Kingdom stands four square with Kuwait in the defence of its independence and its territorial integrity," Rifkind told reporters at the Foreign Office.
Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Jaber al-Sabah, who stopped in London for talks en route to New York, stood alongside Rifkind as he made his comments.
The two met shortly after U.S. President Bill Clinton said in Washington that he had signed an order to deploy 3,500 U.S. ground troops in Kuwait as part of an American military build-up in the Gulf.
Asked whether Britain, which participated in the U.S.-led coalition that drove occupying Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in 1991, was also ready to send troops, Rifkind replied:
"If there was a need for that, if there was perceived to be a threat to Kuwait that required international action, then the United Kingdom would always be prepared to play its full part.
"We've shown in the past the willingness if necessary for troops to be sent. If it became necessary in the future we would also respond in a positive way."

Most of the Arab world has withheld its support for the cruise missile attacks Washington launched on Iraqi targets on September 3 and 4 in retaliation for Saddam's thrust into northern Iraq. But Britain gave firm backing to the strikes.
